target_customer: Data center, industrial and utility buyers of compact nuclear power
problem: Conventional reactors are huge and slow to build; Apollo shrinks the steam generator to make factory-built, truck-transportable reactors.
business_model: Sale of factory-built compact reactors and power (A-10, A-50, A-300 planned)

founders.name: Assil Halimi
founders.background_notes: YC page: reactor operator at Engie, advanced reactor designer at EDF; worked on PWR development with Westinghouse, NuScale and Rolls-Royce per YC page.

founders.name: Drew Walker
education: George Washington University, B.A. political science

competitors.name: Radiant
competitors.traction_then: Building demonstration at Idaho National Lab

competitors.name: Aalo Atomics
competitors.traction_then: Reached criticality in DOE program per later report

technical_complexity.rationale: Nuclear reactor design with NRC licensing, new steam generator geometry and a 1 MW demonstrator still to be built.

defensibility.rationale: Licensing, technical know-how and capital intensity are barriers, though several funded rivals pursue small reactors.

takeover_risk_then.outcome: Incumbents were pursuing SMRs; no sign they copied the compact steam generator approach. Well-funded startups are the main competition.

market_need_then: AI data center power demand and policy support drove record advanced nuclear investment in 2025. Apollo claims over 20 GW of signed letters of intent (company claim, non-binding).

identity.voice_and_tone: Punchy fragments, mission driven (The Energy Future Isn't Coming. It's Being Built.)

brand_strength.rationale: Apollo evokes the moon program and ambition, but origin is not sourced. Strong press pickup followed the funding, and the brand name is reasonably distinctive within nuclear.

outcome_analysis: Apollo Atomics raised a $31M seed in August 2026 within months of its Spring 2026 batch, led by FCVC with YC, Paul Graham and others. Success drivers are a PhD founder with reactor experience, an MIT spinout technology and a strong AI power demand tailwind. The key risks are demonstrator delivery in 2027, NRC licensing and well-funded rivals.
notes: Pulse2 dates the announcement Aug 26 2026 and NEI Aug 24 2026. RuntimeWire reports $26M seed plus $5M debt, conflicting with two outlets stating $31M seed; recorded as $31M seed. Aggregators list a $500K pre-seed, unverified. Total funding coverage may be incomplete (YC deal not recorded).
